what: The CRATE-LEVEL interning ids this chain's aggregate types and FUNCTIONS carry in the emitted artifact, keyed by the canonical FIRST-USE index the core module uses -- and, new in kind with this chain, WHICH of those functions the module DEFINES.
why: Read ir_h2.tags.json's `why` first. This is the FIRST chain whose module holds TWO functions: `has_loose_bvars` is `(func 0 ...)` and the callee `loose_bvar_range` is `(func 1 ...)`, and `ir_call_exec` resolves the call site through `ir_func_find` because the callee is DEFINED rather than merely named. That makes this table load-bearing in a way no earlier one is: the emitted text of the caller names its callee by whole-crate INDEX (`call @func.3657`) and its own id NOT AT ALL, and the callee's text names its own id not at all either. Nothing in either text says that the two indices are the two functions of one module, or which is which. Reader A, which reads the artifact binary, can see it; reader B cannot. This table is how reader B is told.
how_it_is_used: `ir_mint::project` splits the emitted text into exactly the bodies `extra_bodies` declares (plus the root), reads each with its own canonical index PINNED and the chain's whole function namespace pre-seeded, checks each against its own `interface` object, and splices the results into one core module. `ir_mint::mint` reads the aggregate lanes for the alias line, `extra_bodies` for the second body's Clean name prefix, and refuses a module whose function list is not exactly the declared bodies in declared order.
producer_pin: This chain POSTDATES generated/ir_mint.producer_ab.json, so unlike the eleven original rows it has no THREE-producer invariance record. It has TWO reader-A dumps, and they are enough to measure the drift class on this chain rather than inherit it: laneREG wc-REG/dump_O3 2026-08-21 (sha256 af1597c4dffc1f722044457232caeacdf7f02c74bcfe5db7ff95314314c6c4cc) has the caller at @func.3650 (functy.432) and the callee at @func.3649 (functy.430); laneF8 wc-ctl/dump_O3 2026-08-23 (sha256 84b723b8bcf40c02427b13c007d530f28d23b2f504db168f1c7584472077db6e) has them at @func.3665 (functy.438) and @func.3664 (functy.436). ALL FOUR indices moved and the projected core module is BYTE-IDENTICAL. The COMMITTED FIXTURES are a THIRD era (caller @func.3658 functy.435, callee @func.3657 functy.433) with the instruction text byte-identical to both. The pins below are the FIXTURE-ERA ids, because reader B reads the fixture; reader A's are RECORDED in ir_hlb.mint.json and NEVER COMPARED, like observed_ty. The NAMES did not move.
interface_what: The artifact facts the CORE MODULE cannot hold and the emitted text does print, PER BODY. Read `ir_h2.tags.json`'s `interface_what` for why they are pinned here rather than in the module. The `interface` object below is the ROOT body's; each row of `extra_bodies` carries its own. The sharp slot on both bodies is the same one: the by-value receiver `bb0(%0: struct.29)`. `ExprMeta` is a u64 NEWTYPE passed by value, which is why no heap premise appears anywhere in this chain -- and the core module keeps only the SSA id, so this row is the only witness that the receiver is an aggregate rather than a bare u64.
interface_producer_invariance: `ty` is the CANONICAL form; `observed_ty` is the verbatim token and is RECORDED, NEVER COMPARED. `struct.29` resolves through the `structs` lane to `struct#0`. Reader A's own record on the laneREG wc-REG dump_O3 2026-08-21 dump, over BOTH bodies: `param_tys_erased: ["Struct(StructId(29))", "Struct(StructId(29))"]`, `block_param_tys_erased: []`, `aligns_erased: []`.
